note: Outside the stated ICP, and the clearest qualification failure in the batch. Successful is a miss on the criterion as written: a retired high school music teacher and former professional musician and lifeguard, now working 40-50 hours a week for a boss in a role nobody established, which is not a business owner, physician or equivalent. Income is an emphatic miss — 'there's no way I can afford 6,000', debts outstanding, a mortgage running another year, and an expectation of paying $30-40 a month. Good to great is a miss: he is 100 lb above his high school weight and 50 lb above his own target, and the whole framing is recovery of a former self after COVID knocked him down. Two criteria do land. Health genuinely is his neglected area rather than a crisis — career, house and family are all in order, and he has no acute condition. And he clears the exclusion comfortably: 10,000-20,000 steps a day, kayaking, swimming, a YMCA membership he actually uses, so not gym-averse by any reading, and 50 lb above an aspirational target rather than clinically far gone. The finding worth carrying forward is upstream of the ICP entirely. No setter is named on this call, the lead came through an inbound application, and no price framing occurred, so a prospect who expected a $30-a-month membership reached a $6,000 closing call and consumed fifty-three minutes. Whatever screening produced the Rudolph call, where the setter had already pre-framed cost, did not happen here.
